## Crown-cash requests for Arad and a report of banknote shortage

**Sources on this page:** p219 A1, p219 A2, p219 B.

<a id="edition-cases-finance-crown-cash-requests-crown-cash-requests-for-arad-and-a-report-of-banknote-shortage"></a>



**Source edition and recovery: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Childs p219 contains a two-part request about an advance for Arad,
following an arrangement with the German military mission at Budapest,
and a separate message reporting partial crown remittances and a severe
shortage of banknotes. The baseline edition preserves the published labels;
a later treaty-based interpretation identifies both army addresses as 11.

<a id="edition-cases-finance-crown-cash-requests-the-11th-army-addresses"></a>

### The 11th-Army addresses

The [Article XII interpretation](../../experiments/nov25_treaty_digits/README.md)
assigns the received pair `FX` to 1 throughout the Nov25–28 traffic. It
gives the following addresses without changing a source coordinate:

| Part | Conditional received field |
| --- | --- |
| A1 | `ETXINTENDX11FIALA` |
| B | `FELDINTENDXAXOXKX11` |

The monetary amounts remain unassigned. The complete propagation and the
unchanged word-repair costs are recorded in the
[joint certificate](../../experiments/nov25_treaty_digits/certificates.json).

The primary source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX
Cipher System*, [printed p219, PDF page 222](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The page heading is 25 November 1918. A is headed
`UKS v BSL (09.40 p.m., November 25th)`, with origin field
`1320 (11/25) 2 TLE`; B has receipt `09.16 p.m., November 27th`
and origin `1800 (11/25)`. Both dates of B are retained.

The [literal fixture](../../experiments/crown_cash_requests/inputs.json)
and [certificate](../../experiments/crown_cash_requests/certificates.json)
provide three source crops, every source coordinate, independent
transposition maps, complete raw-label inventories and exact repair
certificates. The three bodies already appeared as unreviewed OCR-derived
entries in the repository's
[`p73_new_methods/retrieval_inputs.json`](../../experiments/p73_new_methods/retrieval_inputs.json).
The contribution here is the visually checked source edition and its
reversible repairs, not first computation of those candidate bodies.

<a id="edition-cases-finance-crown-cash-requests-a1-funds-for-arad"></a>

### A1: funds for Arad

All 334 source coordinates are valid. Their raw 167-position reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
ETXINTENDXJJFIALAXXNACHVEREINBARUNGMXDERDTXMILXMISSIONBUDAPESTOBLTXKUDELSOLLENAUSSERDENDORTANGEFORDERTEN6MILXKRONENNOCH3YYYYYKRONENFUERMG0ARADZURVERFGXGESTELLTWERDENXX
```

</details>

The candidate changes only `MG0` to `MGD`, at one observed coordinate:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
ETXINTENDXJJFIALAXXNACHVEREINBARUNGMXDERDTXMILXMISSIONBUDAPESTOBLTXKUDELSOLLENAUSSERDENDORTANGEFORDERTEN6MILXKRONENNOCH3YYYYYKRONENFUERMGDARADZURVERFGXGESTELLTWERDENXX
```

</details>

The address contains `ET. INTEND. JJ FIALA`. The message cites an
arrangement with the German military mission at Budapest, followed by
`OBLT. KUDEL`, and requests that an additional amount labelled
`3YYYYY` crowns be made available for `MGD ARAD`, beyond the amount
labelled `6 MIL` already requested there. The received names `FIALA`
and `KUDEL` are not identified with particular historical people.
The army label `JJ` and both amount labels remain unassigned.

The fifth row ends in the complete group `FDDFX`. The final `X`, which
the earlier OCR treated as uncertain, is observed in the source and gives
a complete `KRONEN` reading. It is not a filled ciphertext erasure.

<a id="edition-cases-finance-crown-cash-requests-a2-can-an-advance-be-drawn"></a>

### A2: can an advance be drawn?

All 230 coordinates are valid. The raw 115-position reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
ERBITTENDRAHTANTWORTOBVORSCHUSSBISZUDIESERHOEHEAUSDORTXFELDKRIEGSKASSEERFORDERLXZEITPBGEHOBENWEGDENKANNXXMGDXARPDXX
```

</details>

Three observed-coordinate changes yield:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
ERBITTENDRAHTANTWORTOBVORSCHUSSBISZUDIESERHOEHEAUSDORTXFELDKRIEGSKASSEERFORDERLXZEITABGEHOBENWERDENKANNXXMGDXARADXX
```

</details>

A telegraphic reply is requested on whether an advance up to that amount
can be drawn from the local field war cash office at the required time.
The received abbreviated wording `ERFORDERL X ZEIT` is retained without
adding a preposition or lengthening the text.

Two complementary readings within these explicitly numbered parts
support the office/place candidate. A2 contains unchanged `MGD`, while
A1 contains unchanged `ARAD`. They support the separate emendations
`MG0 → MGD` in A1 and `ARPD → ARAD` in A2 if the parts refer to the same
office and place. This is within-message contextual support, not an
independent exact retransmission. The abbreviation `MGD` is not expanded.

| Untouched support | Plaintext indices | Original source indices for each pair |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A2 `MGD` | 105–107 | M: 139,99; G: 199,9; D: 159,179 |
| A1 `ARAD` | 138–141 | A: 303,128; R: 84,200; A: 143,288; D: 12,230 |

The complete source coordinates and the separately priced target changes
are included in the certificate.

<a id="edition-cases-finance-crown-cash-requests-b-partial-remittances-and-a-shortage-of-banknotes"></a>

### B: partial remittances and a shortage of banknotes

All 354 coordinates are valid. The raw 177-position reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
FELDINTENDXAXOXKXJJXXZUJ3Y20AUFDORTIGEKRONENANFORDERUNGDRAHTETKMXXKRONENBETRPEGETEILWEISEUEBERWIESENXRESTFOLGTNACHMOEGLICHK9ITXGROSSERNOTENMANGELXXXGENXINTENDANTXROEM4BJ411XJYJ2
```

</details>

Two observed-coordinate repairs restore `BETRAEGE` and `MOEGLICHKEIT`:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
FELDINTENDXAXOXKXJJXXZUJ3Y20AUFDORTIGEKRONENANFORDERUNGDRAHTETKMXXKRONENBETRAEGETEILWEISEUEBERWIESENXRESTFOLGTNACHMOEGLICHKEITXGROSSERNOTENMANGELXXXGENXINTENDANTXROEM4BJ411XJYJ2
```

</details>

The message addresses `FELDINTEND. A. O. K. JJ`, cites `J3Y20`, and
reports a `KM` telegram that crown amounts have partly been remitted,
with the remainder to follow as possible. It explicitly mentions a
severe shortage of banknotes. The received closing field is
`GEN. INTENDANT. ROEM4BJ411XJYJ2`; the labels and abbreviation are not
expanded into a person, date or departmental number.

A and B concern crown liquidity, but the source does not establish that
B answers this particular A request. The common page and compatible
subject are insufficient to equate their transactions. Nor does a
report of partial remittance establish that the whole requested amount
was ultimately paid.

<a id="edition-cases-finance-crown-cash-requests-all-numerical-looking-labels-remain-visible"></a>

### All numerical-looking labels remain visible

The amount labels are fully observed and untouched by any candidate repair:

| Field | Plaintext index | Raw label | Pair | Original source indices |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| A1, `6 MIL` | 104 | 6 | DX | 125, 81 |
| A1, first amount character | 119 | 3 | VV | 257, 97 |
| A1, second amount character | 120 | Y | DG | 213, 53 |
| A1, third amount character | 121 | Y | DG | 156, 316 |
| A1, fourth amount character | 122 | Y | DG | 68, 243 |
| A1, fifth amount character | 123 | Y | DG | 330, 25 |
| A1, sixth amount character | 124 | Y | DG | 170, 112 |

These zero-based positions show the received pattern, not the historical
values of its characters. Plausibility of a round amount is not used to
assign `Y`, `3` or `6`.

Every occurrence of `0123456789JQY` in all six raw/candidate views is
listed in the certificate: **27** source occurrences and **25** candidate
occurrences. The two removed source occurrences are raw `0` in `MG0`
and raw `9` in `MOEGLICHK9IT`. Both receive explicit coordinate repairs;
neither is concealed from a later key-label study. All amount, name,
army and reference fields declared unchanged have their full observed
pair witnesses certified.

<a id="edition-cases-finance-crown-cash-requests-verification-and-attribution"></a>

### Verification and attribution

There are **918 valid observed coordinates**, **459 raw-label plaintext
positions**, and **six** candidate coordinate substitutions: one in A1,
three in A2 and two in B. There are no missing-coordinate fills, source
erasures, insertions, deletions, reordered blocks or key changes. Every
full candidate reencrypts exactly under the published `Nov25-28` key.
These are counts of fixed raw labels and source-edition repairs, not
newly solved numerical values.

The published key is prior work by George Lasry and colleagues; its
provenance is retained. All three earlier automatic retrieval bodies
are explicitly credited. No explicit discussion of these bodies was
located in the bounded paper, ADFGVX dissertation chapter and cached
55-comment checks; this does not establish universal historical priority.

```bash
python experiments/crown_cash_requests/verify.py --verify
python experiments/crown_cash_requests/verify.py --verify --pdf /path/to/childs.pdf
```

The verifier reconstructs the source mapping independently, checks every
raw position and repair, confirms all unchanged fields and complementary
within-message support, and inventories every numerical-looking label.
The optional PDF check verifies the full source hash and every crop pixel.

## p219 C — Kiev unrest between the Hetman government and an unresolved party; soldiers council neutrality

**Edition context:** p219 C — Kiev unrest and the soldiers' council.

<a id="edition-cases-military-p219-kiev-unrest-p219-c--kiev-unrest-and-the-soldiers-council"></a>



**Conditional recovery: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.** The printed group
alternatives and marked jamming loss reveal a report of impending unrest
in Kiev and a soldiers' council decision for neutrality. The new
`BEVORSTEHENDX` completion joins the previously separated body excerpts;
the shared Y also makes the proposed `MARKOWSKY` signature compatible
with every retained observed coordinate.

<a id="source-p219-c"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-military-p219-kiev-unrest-p219-c"></a>

### p219 C

**Readable German — three excerpts from the zero-substitution lexical completion; intervening clause and footer omitted:**

> Heeresgruppe Kiew. Unruhen zwischen Regierung Hetman und PEDF9?RA. […] Soldatenrat beschloss Neutralitaet.

The report concerns unrest between the Hetman government and the unresolved
name `PEDF9?RA`, and says that a soldiers' council resolved on neutrality.
The incomplete modifier `VORSTEHEND?`, the intervening `7?` field and the
full footer remain visible in the complete streams below. The quotation
uses plaintext spans 0–16, 19–64 and 79–112, all zero-based.

<a id="edition-cases-military-p219-kiev-unrest-current-joint-completion"></a>

### Current joint completion

**Conditional interpretation — continuous body with the PETLJURA proposal;
two observed substitutions and twenty inserted-slot fills:**

*Heeresgruppe Kiew. Unruhen zwischen Regierung Hetman und Petljura bevorstehend. Soldatenrat beschloss Neutralitaet.*

The report says that unrest between the Hetman government and the named
opponent is impending, and that the soldiers' council decided on
neutrality. Petljura remains a separately priced name proposal. Without
those two substitutions, the new clause is still source-compatible and
the received name remains `PEDFJ?RA`.

The [joint completion certificate](../../experiments/nov25_treaty_digits/kiev_completion_certificate.json)
rechecks **all 81 declared source models**. The full word selects the
printed **`GXAFV`** alternative over `GXAGV`: its original F at source
28 and A at 131 give **B** at plaintext position 66. The next half-pair
`?D` admits **E**, and the final `X?` admits separator **X**. Filling
modeled slots **95 with F and 96 with V** completes `BEVORSTEHENDX`.
Both slots already belong to the twenty-five-coordinate jamming gap;
this layer introduces no further missing coordinates or observed changes.

Two minimum models remain, differing only in which copy of the duplicated
initial `XFXDD` supplies the first five retained coordinates. They give
**one identical completed ciphertext and body**. The printed group-choice
question and the duplicate-origin ambiguity are therefore distinct.

The original `AD` pair at plaintext 145, source **73 A and 206 D**, now
gives **`MA?KO?SKY`**. The optional spelling **`MARKOWSKY`** needs two
compatible inserted-slot fills and **zero observed substitutions**, down
from two under the published labels. This is a spelling proposal, not
an independently established personal identity.

| Current conditional scope | Observed substitutions | Total inserted-slot fills | Fixed positions |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `BEVORSTEHENDX`, raw names | 0 | 19 | 137/147 |
| Clause plus `MARKOWSKY` | 0 | 21 | 139/147 |
| Clause plus `PETLJURA` | 2 | 20 | 138/147 |
| Clause plus all three proposed names | 3 | 22 | 140/147 |

The combined version retains the one-coordinate `ODELSA→ODESSA` repair.
Its three observed changes are source **10 V→X, 85 X→F and 155 A→F**.
All compact footer fields remain unresolved where their source or square
values are unknown. These counts use the shared partial square and do
not treat unresolved numeral labels as historically established digits.

<a id="edition-cases-military-p219-kiev-unrest-earlier-recovery-layers"></a>

### Earlier recovery layers

The earlier selected frame fixes **122/147 raw published-label positions**.
Seventeen inserted-slot fills give **139/147** with zero observed-coordinate
substitutions. Its complete streams and the separately priced original
name proposals remain below.

The later [shared-square reading](../../experiments/nov25_treaty_digits/README.md#the-kiev-report-outside-the-original-snapshot)
reduces the optional `PETLJURA` spelling from four to **two observed-coordinate changes**.
The received name becomes `PEDFJ?RA` under the independently proposed
`VD=J` assignment. Reading its remaining damaged letters as `PETLJURA`
keeps the same 18 inserted-slot fills and all four minimum source models
at that J-only stage, before the new complete-word constraint.
The two preserved source coordinates are V at index 181 and D at 212;
the remaining substitutions are V→X at 10 and A→F at 155.

<a id="edition-cases-military-p219-kiev-unrest-printed-alternatives-and-jamming"></a>

### Printed alternatives and jamming

The source contains 284 coordinate observations and advertises `RICHI-294`.
It prints three parenthesized groups, a repeated initial `XFXDD`, and a
`(jammed)` note with no stated length. The model retains those observations
as data and tests how to use them in the cipher frame.

`{JAMMED}` in the transcription marks the original `(jammed)` annotation;
the braces are a boundary marker, not coordinate observations.

The earlier selected model excludes source 0–4 (one duplicate), 25–29 (parenthesized
`GXAFV`) and 200–204 (`VDGDD`, choosing its parenthesized `VDFDD` alternative).
The later parenthesized `FXVDD` remains in sequence. Twenty-five unknown
slots are inserted at the printed jamming boundary before original source
85. The model has 294 coordinates and uses the published Nov25–28 key.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 294-slot frame; all 25 added coordinates unassigned:**

```text
HEER?SGRU?PEXKIE?XXUN?UHENX?WISC?ENXREG?ERUN?XHETM?NXUN?XPEDF9?RAX7?VORST?HEND?SOLDAT?NRAT?BESCH?OSSX?EUTRAL?TAET?X7XVX?XODELSA?RM1?3230TMA?KO?SKQX
```

**Edited output — same conditional frame; zero observed substitutions and 17 inserted-slot fills; eight positions unresolved:**


</details>

Choosing the printed `VDFDD` alternative matters: its surviving half-pair
permits E in `HEERESGRUPPE`. The other printed group would require a
separately priced coordinate change for that E. The primary edition fills
only compatible erased half-pairs and preserves the remaining labels.

### Complete declared source-model check

For each parenthesized group the check retains both observations, retains
the preceding group only, or retains the parenthesized group only. It also
retains both initial duplicates or excludes either copy: **27 × 3 = 81 maps**.
Each model adds enough unknown slots at the marked jamming boundary to reach
294 coordinates.

In the earlier comparison, four maps attain the primary template's
zero-substitution minimum. The
combined optional names also have four minimum maps, at seven substitutions.
Both scopes retain two edited streams: an opaque field reads `7?` or `B?`
depending on the first printed alternative. All prices, origins and streams
are retained. The templates leave that field unconstrained rather than using
it to choose a historical label.

<a id="edition-cases-military-nov25-provisions-and-evening-report"></a>

## p219 D1 — First part: reduced provisioning strength and no further provisions

**Edition context:** Reduced provisioning strength and a separate evening report.

**Related source pages:** [p220 A2](220.md#source-p220-a2), [p220 B](220.md#source-p220-b).

<a id="edition-cases-military-nov25-provisions-and-evening-report-reduced-provisioning-strength-and-a-separate-evening-report"></a>



**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Two physically numbered parts request a complete stop to provisions after
a reduction in the strength being provisioned. The existing shared-square
interpretation identifies their army field as **11th Army**. Their association
is explicit across the p219/p220 page break. A separate evening report on
p220 now supports **Tiszafoeldvar, Nagymagocs and Kondoros** as places reached,
while its unit labels remain incomplete. All three retain their complete
native printed frames.

<a id="source-p219-d1"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-military-nov25-provisions-and-evening-report-p219-d1"></a>

### p219 D1

**Source transcription — header:** `D) UKS v ZÖN (10.11 p.m., November 25th); 1849 2 TLE; 1 TL RICHI-166`

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — every native source slot in printed order, with non-coordinate glyphs masked:**

```text
INFOLGEVERRINGERTERXVERPFLEGUNGSSTAERKEFUERJJXARMEEKEINEVERPFLEGNNGFEHRERFOGDERLICH
```

**Edited output — 3 observed-coordinate substitutions and 0 source-mask fills; no insertion, deletion or reordering:**

```text
INFOLGEVERRINGERTERXVERPFLEGUNGSSTAERKEFUERJJXARMEEKEINEVERPFLEGUNGMEHRERFORDERLICH
```

**Readable German — exact nonseparator labels of the edited output:**

> Infolge verringerter Verpflegungsstaerke fuer JJ. Armee keine Verpflegung mehr erforderlich.

</details>

**Conditional interpretation — existing shared FX=1 interpretation and the same three word repairs:**

> Infolge verringerter Verpflegungsstaerke fuer 11. Armee keine Verpflegung mehr erforderlich.

**Meaning:** Under the existing shared-square interpretation, the message
states that the 11th Army's reduced provisioning strength makes further
provisions unnecessary. The next part requests an immediate, complete
halt to further supplies.

The two original `FX` pairs at plaintext positions 43–44 come from
source **10 F + 83 X** and **53 F + 133 X**. Neither was touched by the
three word repairs. Their `11` reading follows the already supported
`FX=1` assignment; this passage introduces no new numeral choice or
source change. The [separate follow-up certificate](../../experiments/nov25_evening_place_witness/certificate.json)
checks both pairs and the complete current quotation.

**Editorial limits:**

- All 166 observed coordinates are present, including the final printed VGGXA F omitted by the earlier 160-coordinate OCR block. Restoring those visible coordinates is a transcription correction, not a hypothetical lost-prefix or missing-slot fill.
- The word proposals VERPFLEGNNG → VERPFLEGUNG, FEHR → MEHR and ERFOGDERLICH → ERFORDERLICH have explicit observed-coordinate costs. All raw garbles remain displayed.
- JJ remains literal in both earlier label streams above. The separately certified shared-square interpretation supplies 11 in the current reading; no headcount or additional key assignment is inferred.
- The printed continued marker, identical UKS/ZÖN routing, 10.11 p.m. interception, 1849 internal reference and 2 TLE count associate this first part with p220 A2. The source changes its section label from D to A across the page break.

<a id="edition-cases-military-nov25-provisions-and-evening-report-source-and-scope"></a>

### Source and scope

[Childs source](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view) · [Reviewed p219 excerpt](../../experiments/nov25_provisions_and_evening_report/sources/p219_reviewed.png) · [Reviewed p220 excerpt](../../experiments/nov25_provisions_and_evening_report/sources/p220_reviewed.png) · [Inputs](../../experiments/nov25_provisions_and_evening_report/inputs.json) · [Position and change certificates](../../experiments/nov25_provisions_and_evening_report/certificates.json)

### Evidence, credit and reproduction

Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier repository OCR and unchanged-key outputs are retained separately. Source review and explicit editorial work: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.

The certificates independently reconstruct column positions and domains, compare them with the cipher implementation, replay every priced change, and check all readable nonseparator labels. Partial readings have one consistent injective square/source-mask completion witness that re-encrypts exactly; those witness choices are not historical identifications. Source images are bound to the original PDF by page, rectangle, scale, file digest and pixel digest.

Reproduce with `python experiments/nov25_provisions_and_evening_report/verify.py --verify`. Add `--pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf` to check the original PDF and exact source-crop pixels.

### p220 A2

**Source transcription — header:** `A) UKS v ZÖN (10.11 p.m., November 25th); 1849 2 TLE; 2 TL RICHI-244`

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — every native source slot in printed order, with non-coordinate glyphs masked:**

```text
BITTENACHSCHUBANVERPFLEGUNGSOFOR3GANZEINSTELLENXGLEICHESTELEGRAMMGEHTANGENENALINTENDANTUNDPROVIANTDEPOTDRESDENXXVIERAXU203
```

**Edited output — 2 observed-coordinate substitutions and 0 source-mask fills; no insertion, deletion or reordering:**

```text
BITTENACHSCHUBANVERPFLEGUNGSOFORTGANZEINSTELLENXGLEICHESTELEGRAMMGEHTANGENERALINTENDANTUNDPROVIANTDEPOTDRESDENXXVIERAXU203
```

</details>

**Readable German — exact nonseparator labels of the edited output:**

> Bitte Nachschub an Verpflegung sofort ganz einstellen. Gleiches Telegramm geht an Generalintendant und Proviantdepot Dresden. VIERA. U203.

**Meaning:** The continuation requests an immediate, complete halt to further provisions and states that the same telegram goes to the Generalintendant and the provisions depot at Dresden. It records a request and notification, without proving that deliveries actually stopped. The closing labels VIERA and U203 remain unexpanded.

**Editorial limits:**

- The complete native 244-coordinate body matches its header. Two earlier OCR blocks split this one physical source part; neither block alone gives its full geometry.
- SOFOR3 → SOFORT and GENENALINTENDANT → GENERALINTENDANT are separately priced ordinary-word proposals, with no global reinterpretation of the 3 label.
- VIERA and U203 remain literal closing fields. They are not silently converted to an office, a personal name, a number or an expanded date.
- The source explicitly marks this as part 2 and repeats the p219 D header. Its association with that first part is supported by printed metadata as well as the continued marker, not solely by similar meaning.

<a id="edition-cases-military-nov25-provisions-and-evening-report-a-shared-letter-identifies-nagymágocs"></a>

#### A shared letter identifies Nagymágocs

The later [shared `AD=Y` interpretation](../../experiments/nov25_treaty_digits/README.md#the-shared-y-in-strzemieczny-and-nagymagocs)
turns `NAGQMAGOCS` into **`NAGYMAGOCS`**. At plaintext position 90,
the pair comes from the originally observed **A at source 74 and D at
source 180**. This is the same cell that completes Strzemieczny's surname
in p224 C1; neither name requires an added source-coordinate repair.

The place spelling is independently printed in *Csongrád vármegye
Hivatalos Lapja*, **21 December 1912**, no. 59, p349, items 86–89, in
the municipality's proposed 1913 budgets.
[National-library scan](https://epa.hu/05200/05279/00539/pdf/EPA05279_csongradvarmegye_hivatalos_lapja_1912_059.pdf)
· [Masthead](../../experiments/nov25_treaty_digits/sources/csongrad_1912_title.png)
· [Nagymágocs entries](../../experiments/nov25_treaty_digits/sources/nagymagocs_1912.png).
The newly identified place is one location that leading elements
reportedly reached; the adjacent unit labels remain unresolved. The other
damaged place has the separate native witness described next.
The gazette supplies a geographical spelling, not a separate account
of the reported military movement.

<a id="edition-cases-military-nov25-provisions-and-evening-report-a-native-place-witness-under-a-different-key"></a>

#### A native place witness under a different key

The 30 November evening report [p229 A1](229.md#edition-cases-military-late-transport-dispatches)
directly reads **`TISZAFOELDVAR`** at positions 41–53, using 26 untouched
observed coordinates under its different Nov28–Dec1 key. Its Z is `VX`,
from source 219 V and 148 X. That native spelling supports the earlier
`TISHAFOELDVAR` place repair.

In p220 B, H at position 72 comes from `AA`, source 6 and 150. The
proposed change **6 A→D**, retaining source 150 A, gives `DA=Z`.
The original image visibly has A; this is an observed-coordinate repair,
not a corrected transcription. The older `HABE7→HABEN` repair at source
157 remains separate, for **two total observed substitutions**, no fills
and the unchanged 220-coordinate frame.

**Conditional interpretation — shared Y and the witnessed place spelling, with unit labels retained:**

> Es haben mit Anfaengen erreicht: 21?ID, Tiszafoeldvar. PRD, Nagymagocs. ?21?, Kondoros.

This makes the place list readable as Tiszafoeldvar, Nagymagocs and
Kondoros while preserving its incomplete unit labels. The donor is a
separate later report, not a duplicate reception; it supports the
spelling without establishing this report's unit identities or movements.
The [cross-key place check](../../experiments/nov25_evening_place_witness/README.md)
prices all 98 possible starts of that spelling in the native recipient
frame. Position 69 is the only one-substitution minimum for this fixed
word and frame. The conditional fixed-position count stays **103/110**:
H was already observed, so this repair does not recover an erased position.

**Editorial limits:**

- All 220 observed coordinates remain in their native order. The earlier primary word proposal HABE7 → HABEN is priced as an observed-coordinate change, not as a free reading of a numeral; the new place repair adds one separately recorded change.
- 13, JJ22ALPE, K, 16, 1ZUIGE, 1J0ID, TISHAFOELDVAR, PRD, NAGQMAGOCS81J8 and KONDOROS keep their exact labels. Word spacing in the opening is editorial and does not establish its syntax or reference values.
- The original edition supplies no unit number or geographical correction. Its TISHAFOELDVAR and NAGQMAGOCS remain in the exact label stream. The separate shared-Y interpretation and one-coordinate witnessed repair identify those two places in the current reading.
- The HATTE MR heading contains a 4-like glyph rendered as [4-like] in the metadata. This is a header transcription qualification and does not add a source-ciphertext erasure or a decoded position.
- B has its own source label and reception time. It is not counted as a third part of the two-part provisioning message above.
